Commentary.Commentary: Right then, Australia have got their campaign underway with a win and are building up nicely to that clash against eternal rivals England in a couple of days' time. The only downside was Mitchell Starc hobbling off the playing field but later on it was confirmed as just a cramp which is great news. We have had 10 matches so far and there are still a few teams who haven't yet taken the field, one of them being Pakistan who will play the next game of the tournament against an in-form USA side. That match will be played on Thursday, 6 June in Dallas, Texas and the match will begin at 9 pm IST (3.30 pm GMT) but you can tune in a lot sooner for the build-up. Cheers!

The victorious skipper of Australia, Mitchell Marsh says to begin the tournament with a victory is always a good thing. Says that the contribution of Marcus Stoinis was key for the side as he took the game deep and kept landing those big shots. Informed that it was just a bit of a cramp for Mitchell Starc and nothing to be worried about. Adds that they are looking forward to playing England next up and they are excited with the wickets being the way they are as a closer game between Oman and Australia is good for the game in the bigger picture.

The captain of Oman, Aqib Ilyas says the tournament is set up good and losing in the Super Over and doing then doing well against a big team is good. Adds that the credit goes to the bowlers and just that one over where Marcus Stoinis got a life and then got 26 off the over changed the game. Mentions that they have good spinners in the side and even the pacers bowl good but it's just that one fielding mishap happened. On his catch, he says that somewhile back, Zeeshan Maqsood took one stellar catch and he wanted to replicate that and wanted to do something magical against the Aussies. Adds that they changed their plans and tried to bowl away from the slot but it was a bit late and goes on to say that they have quality batters and it is just the big occasion that has got the better of them. Ends by saying that they are looking forward to the next game against Scotland who are a team they have played against quite a lot.

Marcus Stoinis is the Player of the Match for his fine all-round showing. He says that it is a nice start and they are happy to get the win and everybody got to bowl. Adds that he was looking to hit the ball hard along the ground and then he picked his bowlers and took them on. Mentions that it was a bit harder to face the spinners rather than the pacers as the ball was keeping up and down for them more. Adds that he bowled a lot of cross seemed deliveries as the balls were keeping low occasionally so he tried to mix it with the bouncers as well.
The Presentation ceremony...

Oman will look back at this game and they will think that they could have really pushed Australia down to the wire in this game but that's where the difference between the top teams and the rest of the pack lies, they make you pay even if you give them half a chance. Oman were brilliant with the ball for about two-thirds of the game and then with the bat as well, the middle order and even the tail managed to get some big hits away. They simply lost too many wickets in the Powerplay which pegged them back and from there on, it was always going to be a bridge too far. Ayaan Khan starred with a 36-run knock and Mehran Khan got a fine cameo of 27 runs from jsut 16 balls as Oman managed to avoid getting bundled out and scored a few useful runs towards the end.

Having put on 164 runs on the back of a scintillating knock from Marcus Stoinis and a gritty fifty from David Warner, Australia managed to pick up wickets in the Powerplay. Mitchell Starc was upbeat after a fine few performances at the backend of the Indian T20 League and picked up a wicket in the first over and set the tone for the rest of the bowlers. Marcus Stoinis followed his heroics with the bat by picking up a couple of quick wickets and the Adam Zampa followed it up with a couple of wickets of his own. Zampa did get hit for a few boundaries and so did Josh Hazlewood but by then the damage had been done. Stoinis finished with three wickets and became only the third player in a Men's T20 World Cup game to score a fifty and pick three wickets as Nathan Ellis closed out the innings with a couple of wickets to his name as well.

Australia are up and running in their quest to hold three major Men's international accolades at the same time having already bagged the World test Championship and the ODI World Cup last year but it was a hard-fought win against a gritty Oman side. It might look straightforward on paper given the 39-run victory margin but the Aussies had to dig deep, especially with the bat to get this win.

Lovely length, just a bit full and on off stump, this one pitches and seams away off the deck. Aqib Ilyas is drawn forward but the ball isn't all that full and the seam movement means the outside edge is found. The ball nestles into the mitts of Matthew Wade behind the stumps and Oman have lost their third wicket at the end of the Powerplay.
Commentary.Howout: c Matthew Wade b Marcus Stoinis
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Marcus Stoinis to Aqib Ilyas, OUT! c Matthew Wade b Marcus Stoinis.

Commentary.Commentary: Nice and full outside the off stump, Aqib Ilyas leans ahead and plays it towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Marcus Stoinis to Aqib Ilyas, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Aqib Ilyas giving Marcus Stoinis a taste of his own medicine and that has landed just beyond the pool. Short of a length and outside off, Aqib Ilyas shuffles across to the off side and pulls it away a bit flat and over deep square leg for a maximum.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Marcus Stoinis to Aqib Ilyas, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Good length around the top of off stump, tight line and Aqib Ilyas can only blocks it towards mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Marcus Stoinis to Aqib Ilyas, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nagging length in and around the off stump, Aqib Ilyas is late on the shot and gets an outside edge to short third. Aqib Ilyas once again looks to setal a single but is sent back as the fielder misses the direct hit at the keeper's end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Marcus Stoinis to Aqib Ilyas, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts off with a floated delivery and gets it right at the toes, Aqib Ilyas jams the ball down to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Marcus Stoinis to Aqib Ilyas, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length, right around the top of off and middle, Zeeshan Maqsood gets well on the front foot and firmly blocks it to the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Nathan Ellis to Zeeshan Maqsood, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Zeeshan Maqsood walks out at 4 for Oman.

OUT! LBW! Looked dead straight and the finger is raised after the appeal! There were two noises though and Kashyap Prajapati has taken the review. Nathan Ellis dishes out the quicker one again and bowls it full on middle, angling it back in. Kashyap Prajapati looks to clear the front leg and heave across the line but seems to be beaten on the inside edge. The third umpire is called in and there's no bat involved as Ball Tracking comes up with umpire's call on the wickets and the onfield decision will stand.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Nathan Ellis to Kashyap Prajapati, OUT! lbw b Nathan Ellis.

Commentary.Commentary: Another slower one but this is pitched up on the stumps, Kashyap Prajapati watchfully blocks it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Nathan Ellis to Kashyap Prajapati, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kashyap Prajapati is going nowhere at the moment. Nathan Ellis displaying all his skills as he brings out the sloeer bumper now and bowls it around off stump. This one comes in at helmet height and Kashyap Prajapati is well beaten as he looks to hook it away.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Nathan Ellis to Kashyap Prajapati, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The quicker one now, bowled on a hard length around middle and gets it to shoot off the deck, Kashyap Prajapati is taken aback and gets hit on the gloves.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Nathan Ellis to Kashyap Prajapati, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts off with a back-of-the-hand slower ball, bowls it into the pitch and around off, Aqib Ilyas dabs it down in front of point and picks up a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Nathan Ellis to Aqib Ilyas, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nathan Ellis replaces Mitchell Starc (2-0-17-1).
Beaten again! A bit full and in the channel around off, shaping away beautifully. Kashyap Prajapati plants his front leg across to guide it away but the ball goes past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Josh Hazlewood to Kashyap Prajapati, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length and around off stump, Kashyap Prajapati stays back and nudges it down on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Josh Hazlewood to Kashyap Prajapati, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! Nice and full around the off stump, nipping away off the deck, Kashyap Prajapati looks to play at it but the ball zips past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Josh Hazlewood to Kashyap Prajapati, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short again and around the hips, Aqib Ilyas whips it nicely and down to fine leg for just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Josh Hazlewood to Aqib Ilyas, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower delivery, on a length and outside off, Aqib Ilyas goes across the off stump and looks to scoop it away but is well beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Josh Hazlewood to Aqib Ilyas, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Banged in quick and short at the batter, hurrying on, Kashyap Prajapati whips it away down to deep backward square leg for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Josh Hazlewood to Kashyap Prajapati, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wow, a comedy of errors out there in the middle and eventually, Aqib Ilyas survives. Full and shaping into the pads, Aqib Ilyas misses the tuck and the ball goes off the pads in front of square leg. Ilyas wants the run but is left stranded midway on the crease. Travis Head there picks up the ball but ends up just lobbing a throw at the keeper's end which Matthew Wade is unable to collect. Glenn Maxwell who is backing up pick up the ball and under-arms it on the stumps. The replays though show that Ilyas had made it back by then.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Mitchell Starc to Aqib Ilyas, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Mid off was well wide but that is a lovely shot from Aqib Ilyas. Pitched up around off stump, Ilyas just leans on and strokes it with the full face of the bat down to the long off fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Mitchell Starc to Aqib Ilyas, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: That should have been put away! Full and wide outside off, a low full toss, Aqib Ilyas reaches out and slaps it straight to the man at cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Mitchell Starc to Aqib Ilyas, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that was the ball that can trouble any batter. Nice and full on the stumps, swinging back in so late, Aqib Ilyas does well to get bat first on that one as the ball ends up thudding on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Mitchell Starc to Aqib Ilyas, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Drags the length back a bit and spills it down the leg side for another wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Mitchell Starc to Aqib Ilyas, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Good length around leg stump and skidding through, Kashyap Prajapati misses the flick and the ball goes off the thigh pad just to the leg side. The batters scamper across for a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Mitchell Starc to Kashyap Prajapati, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up around the middle stump, Kashyap Prajapati solidly blocks it off with a straight bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Mitchell Starc to Kashyap Prajapati, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a hard length and outside off stump, Kashyap Prajapati plays it late and just guides it past a diving Glenn Maxwell at first slip down to third man for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Josh Hazlewood to Kashyap Prajapati, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: The inside edge saves him! Full and around off, getting it to shape back in, Kashyap Prajapati falls over a bit as he looks to flick and gets a big inside edge back onto the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Josh Hazlewood to Kashyap Prajapati, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on a tight line around off stump, Kashyap Prajapati stands tall and taps it down to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Josh Hazlewood to Kashyap Prajapati, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length and in the channel outside off stump, Kashyap Prajapati watches it well and shoulders arms at it. You don't see that often in T20 cricket!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Josh Hazlewood to Kashyap Prajapati, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes even fuller and bowls it outside off, Aqib Ilyas squeezes the drive of the outside half of the bat down to third man and picks up a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Josh Hazlewood to Aqib Ilyas, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts from over the wicket and pitches the ball right up to the off stump, Aqib Ilyas stays watchful and plays it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Josh Hazlewood to Aqib Ilyas, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Josh Hazlewood will bowl from the other end.
End of a long and engrossing first over and Oman are 12/1 at the end of it. Full and wide outside off, thrashed away on the up wide of mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Mitchell Starc to Aqib Ilyas, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good review! Another appeal for LBW and this time, the finger goes up. Aqib Ilyas has reviewed it pretty quickly. On a fullish lenght at 141.4 clicks and swinging back in from leg stump, Aqib Ilyas misses the flick and gets hit on the pads, this one seems to be shaping down the leg side. No bat involved and Ball Tracking shows that it was pitching outside leg stump and the onfield call is overturned. NOT OUT!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Mitchell Starc to Aqib Ilyas, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! That is wayward from Mitchell Starc as he now goes full and wide, slanting it well beyond the tramline outside off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Mitchell Starc to Aqib Ilyas, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Uppish but in the gap! Too full and wide outside off, looking for the magic delivery but this one doesn't swing back in. Aqib Ilyas goes after it and gets it square past cover-point as the ball trickles away into the fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Mitchell Starc to Aqib Ilyas, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Aqib Ilyas walks out to bat at 3.

OUT! LBW! A brute of a delivery from Mitchell Starc as he gets the fuller one to swing back in late from middle stump. Pratik Athavale looks to jam it out but seems to have got an inside edge onto the pads. A huge appeal for LBW but the umpire says no. Was it pad first? There were two noises and eventually, Mitchell Marsh does take the review. The replays though show that it was pad first and Ball Tracking comes up with three reds. Pratik Athavale departs for a golden duck and Starc is underway in his very first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Mitchell Starc to Pratik Athavale, OUT! lbw b Mitchell Starc.

Commentary.Commentary: Much more like it from Mitchell Starc. Full on leg stump, swinging in late onto the toes, Kashyap Prajapati nudges it away in front of square leg and picks up a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Mitchell Starc to Kashyap Prajapati, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Overcorrection from Mitchell Starc as he gets it full and well down the leg side for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Mitchell Starc to Kashyap Prajapati, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Oh, that is a lovely, lovely shot to get the run chase underway! Nice and full, shaping back in from around off stump, Kashyap Prajapati covers the off stump and plays a checked drive through cover-point and the ball races away to the fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Mitchell Starc to Kashyap Prajapati, Four!
